title: Karol G Reveals New Album’s Tracklist Features Collabs With Drake, Bruno Mars & More - Billboard
content:
The Colombian artist will drop her sixth studio set, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, soon. Karol G has unveiled the tracklist of her sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which is set to drop Friday (Aug. 7). The Colombian artist revealed the song titles in an Instagram post Wednesday (Aug. 5) that featured a baby blue back cover showing a relaxed looking Karol G with her hair flowing around her face. Over the image are the 14 titles alongside the names of featured artists — in order — Drake on “Ahí,” Bruno Mars on “Still,” Judeline and Rusowsky on “Bby Wow” and Greg Gonzalez of Cigarettes of Sex on album closer “Después de Ti.” If the title of her new set — which translates to “I Don’t Regret Feeling So Much” — is any indication, the project may be a departure from her 2025 album, the tropical-leaning Tropicoqueta, and a more intimate and vulnerable look at the musician born Carolina Giraldo Navarro. The song names can even attest to all the feeling and passion she poured into this new set, such as “Bebiendo Lagrimas” (“Drinking Tears”), “Alguien Que Te Amaba” (“Someone Who Loved You”) and “¿Con Quién Andará?” (“Who Is He dating?”). Karol first previewed her new era at her headlining Coachella set in April, where she premiered the nostalgic ballad “Después de Tí” with guitarist Gonzalez, powered by a dreamy, glam pop melody grasping on to the memories after dealing with loss and grief.  She later teased the provocative perreo “Matadora” at the kickoff show of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour on July 24 in Chicago’s Soldier Field. The song debuted at No. 3 on the Hot Latin Songs chart dated Aug. 8. And fans may have suspected something could be in the works with the OVO boss when Drake showed up at Karol G’s Toronto show on July 29. Though he didn’t join her on stage at the Rogers Centre, Drizzy did appear on the giant screen, smiling and grooving to her music. Prior to that, Charlamagne Tha God had claimed that the Colombian star was set to appear on Drake’s album ICEMAN, which arrived in May without a collab between the two, though the rapper did give her a shout-out on companion album MAID OF HONOUR‘s “New Bestie.” Check out the No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto tracklist below: Your email address will not be published.

title: GS P&L jumps as strong Q2 and tourism lift outlook in South Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: GS P&L(499790) released second-quarter results that beat market expectations, and shares are surging in early trading as the securities industry projects improved earnings in the second half. At 9:35 a.m. on the 5th, GS P&L was trading at 44,300 won on the KOSPI, up 4,050 won (10.06%) from the previous session. The stock rose as high as 46,450 won during the session. The previous day, GS P&L disclosed that on a consolidation basis, second-quarter revenue was 159 billion won, up 41.7% from a year earlier. Operating profit was 29.4 billion won, up 153.9%, beating market expectations. Net profit was also 19.2 billion won, up 219.6%. An increase in foreign visitors to Korea and higher hotel room rates appear to have driven the improved results. The normalization of operations at the Westin Seoul Parnas and higher occupancy and average spend per guest at Nine Tree Hotel, along with stronger tourism demand in Jeju, also helped boost profitability. The securities industry projected that the earnings growth trend will continue in the third quarter, which enters the peak season. title: GS Caltex to Fully Automate Incheon Lubricant Logistics Center - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
First Fully Four-Way Shuttle at a Korean Hazardous Materials Warehouse
Product Capacity, Speed Expected to Rise More Than 20%
Partnership with Hyundai Glovis; Operations to Begin Early Next Year GS Caltex said on the 5th that it will convert its Incheon Global Lubricant Logistics Center into a fully automated facility. The company plans to introduce a four-way shuttle-type automated storage and retrieval system for the first time at a hazardous materials warehouse in Korea, automating the entire inbound and outbound process starting early next year and enabling high-density logistics operations even in limited space. The four-way shuttle system being introduced moves shuttles in four directions—forward, backward, left and right—inside the rack, automatically storing and retrieving pallets stacked with cargo. Compared with existing one-directional systems, its space utilization is higher, and product capacity within the same area is expected to expand by about 24%. Processing speed is also expected to be 25% faster than manual work, and on-site safety is expected to improve significantly through unmanned operation. GS Caltex, which earns more than half of its lubricant business revenue from exports, pursued the project to secure supply stability and delivery competitiveness in the global market. By applying advanced automation technology, the company aims to overcome the physical limitations of a special hazardous materials environment and drive digital transformation (DX) across logistics operations, raising both operational efficiency and work safety at the same time. Hyundai Glovis (086280) will handle the design of the smart logistics solution and the establishment of the integrated control system. The two companies plan to combine GS Caltex's know-how in hazardous materials logistics operations with Hyundai Glovis's logistics automation capabilities, and to jointly explore expanding the technology into similar logistics environments in the future. "This partnership is a pioneering project that demonstrates the applicability of a four-way shuttle-type automated storage and retrieval system in the special logistics environment of hazardous materials," a GS Caltex official said. "We will begin full-scale operation of the automated global logistics center in early 2027 to further strengthen productivity and safety." Original reporting by Song Ju-hee for Seoul Economic Daily. title: Vikings Training Camp Observations: Testing Depth at Receiver; DBs Make Plays - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — It was a "bluebird day," as some like to say, at TCO Performance Center. The Vikings kept their 2026 Training Camp rolling with fans present Tuesday, and temperatures in the mid-70s as a breeze counteracted the humidity. And even with a teaching focus, the action was spicy. Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy continued to interchange with the first offense, and the younger quarterback seemed to piece together one of his stronger days so far on the grass, highlighted by touchdowns to Gavin Bartholomew, Myles Price and Bryson Nesbit during a low-red zone 7-on-7 period. One of Murray's sharpest pitches of the afternoon was caught over the middle by Jauan Jennings; it featured Murray staying on schedule and zipping the ball into a zone right on Jennings' 6-foot-3 frame. View photos of Vikings players during Training Camp practice on August 4. Before practice, Head Coach Kevin O'Connell said that he really likes the direction the team is headed. "There's always going to be different levels to the competition," O'Connell explained. "Our guys are handling it the right way. One side wins one side of things, another side wins another. But it's [all about the] next play, next period, next practice. We're just kind of in this mindset that we're trying to build right now of totally committing yourself, all 11 guys, both phases, each individual snap, and can we move on? Can we respond? Can we be better on the next play no matter what happened on the previous?" Here are three observations from Day 6 of camp, which included a good mixture of wins for the offense and defense, as well as a ramped-up competitiveness that carried over from a full-pads session Monday. One of the earliest highlights Tuesday involved Justin Jefferson linking with Murray to the right corner during a half-field rep in the red zone that was designed to drill WR spacing out of bunches and stacks. On the very next pass, Murray went to the opposite side and connected with big TE Josh Oliver for six. But once the practice shifted into competitive periods, Jefferson and other starters got some rest. At times, Jennings was WR1. Tai Felton, Price and Jeshaun Jones were involved behind him, and Dontae Fleming and Dillon Bell got work, too. On one occasion, Fleming and McCarthy synced on a Cover 2 hole shot with Bell attracting tight coverage in the flat. Second-year TE Gavin Bartholomew made several strong, contested catches, again, as well, to keep up his stretch of productive days in camp. You'd never guess Chuck Demmings played at FCS-level Stephen F. Austin. He's around the ball too often – for positive reasons – and his play strength is on par with guys from much larger programs. Anyway, let's add "locked-in celebrations" to his focus, faith and freestyle rap. Each aspect of Demmings has been fun to watch/learn about. On Tuesday, "Chucky D" collected a PBU on Felton in the back of the end zone and another PBU on Price on a quick pass to the left. He followed the plays by whipping out LeBron James' "Silencer" celly and a strapping seatbelt celly. Demmings also aggressively pursued Jennings after a short catch to finish practice with a stop by the defense. Undrafted rookie CB Da'Veawn Armstead notched a notable PBU, as well, after sticking with Jennings over the middle on a longer-developing play. The offense – and the quarterbacks – successfully dialed a few quick passes Tuesday. Once, Murray executed a snappy play-fake and found fullback Max Bredeson in the flat to his right. Murray also had a quick connection with Felton, and he snuck one between two defenders to Jones. Two of McCarthy's fastest releases were caught by Bartholomew, including a swift score to the left side. Vikings Training Camp will take place at the Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center. title: Cannonballs discovered during pre-check at G.S. Airport in Gulf Shores & Orange Beach - Mullet Wrapper
content:
Five small 19th-century historic cannonballs stolen from Fort Morgan were discovered wrapped in paper towels in a passenger’s bag during a pre-flight screening at Gulf Shores International Airport on July 18. It was determined that the cannonballs were inert but were not the property of the passenger.
Transportation Security Administration officer Justin Dupree saw what appeared to be a large opaque item on his X-ray screen that he initially thought might be a grapefruit sized medicine ball.
“My first thought was, I couldn’t see a fuse and need to get some help quick. I couldn’t see the entire item but was scared I might have been holding a live explosive,” Dupree said. “I had never seen anything quite this unique. I’ve seen inert grenades and training munitions but never an Indiana Jones-esque stolen artifact-type situation.”
Police determined a juvenile visiting his grandparents placed the cannonballs in his grandparent’s bag, but did not steal the cannonballs. Officials at Fort Morgan State Historic Site did not want to press charges against the juvenile.
“I am very proud of the great catch and teamwork by our officers, the Baldwin County Sheriff’s Office and Gulf Shores Police Department,” said TSA Alabama Federal Security Director Tara Corse. “Even if inert and not active, travelers should avoid bringing weapons of any kind, including replicas, to the airport. They can cause security alerts, flight delays and safety concerns.”

title: GS E&C Jumps 18%, Daewoo E&C 14% on SMR Tax Support, Bill Gates Visit - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Nuclear Stocks Rally as Government Expands National Strategic Technologies
Daewoo E&C's Surprise Earnings Add to Gains Nuclear power and construction-related stocks rallied across the board as the government's expansion of tax support for small modular reactors (SMRs) coincided with anticipation surrounding a visit to Korea by Bill Gates, founder of TerraPower. Daewoo E&C further boosted investor sentiment by reporting second-quarter earnings that exceeded market expectations. According to the Korea Exchange on the 5th, GS E&C closed at 28,750 won based on the previous day's closing price, up 18.56% from the prior trading session. Other nuclear power and construction-related stocks also finished higher, including BHI (16.88%), Hanmi Global (16.51%), Daewoo E&C (14.29%), and Sammi Metal (12.54%). The biggest factor driving up share prices was the government's expansion of tax support. On the 3rd of this month, the government announced its "2026 Tax Reform Plan" and decided to expand the scope of national strategic technologies from the existing hydrogen sector to future energy fields such as SMRs and micro modular reactors (MMRs). As a result, related companies will be able to receive tax credits of 30 to 50% of research and development (R&D) costs and 15 to 30% of facility investment costs. News of the visit to Korea by Bill Gates, founder of TerraPower, also stimulated investor sentiment. Bill Gates is reportedly seeking a meeting with Prime Minister Han Seong-suk, and expectations are growing that, should the meeting take place, key agenda items will include measures to respond to power demand arising from the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and semiconductor clusters, as well as ways to utilize SMRs. Among construction firms, expectations for benefits were most pronounced for GS E&C. Based on its experience building large nuclear power plants, GS E&C is pursuing participation in the SMR business and is also expanding development projects that span the planning, design, construction, and operation of data centers. Daewoo E&C added strong earnings to the mix. The company disclosed that its second-quarter operating profit this year, on a consolidated basis, was 232.3 billion won, up 182.6% from the same period last year. This far exceeded market forecasts. Jang Moon-jun, an analyst at KB Securities, said, "Second-quarter operating profit exceeded market consensus by 38.8%," adding, "Profitability improved significantly, with the cumulative second-quarter gross profit margin (GPM) in the construction segment reaching 21.2%." title: BMW Just Built Its 150,000th Motorcycle In Brazil - bmwblog
content: The company’s largest motorcycle factory outside Germany reached the milestone in just 10 years. BMWBLOG » News » BMW Just Built Its 150,000th Motorcycle In Brazil Although most people associate BMW with cars, the company actually has a longer history of making motorcycles. The R 23 came out in 1923. That’s six years before the 3/15 PS DA 2 became the first car to carry the fabled BMW emblem. More than a century after it assembled its first motorcycle, the company is now celebrating a regional production milestone. BMW Motorrad Brazil just built its 150,000th motorcycle at the Manaus Plant. It just so happens to be the site’s 10th anniversary, with the first bikes rolling off the assembly line in the country’s seventh-largest city in 2016. This R 1300 GS Adventure Triple Black is one of 13 models built at the site, the only plant where the company exclusively builds motorcycles outside Germany. As a refresher, the BMW Group also makes motorcycles in Thailand at the Rayong plant, where more than 20 BMW, MINI, and BMW Motorrad products are assembled for the local and ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) markets. At home in Germany, the company makes motorcycles, scooters, and components at its Berlin plant. BMW prides itself on being the largest motorcycle and scooter producer in the premium segment. It has about 1,300 dealers in approximately 100 countries worldwide. However, 2025 wasn’t a particularly great year for the two-wheeled division, as production fell by 7.4% to 199,736 units while sales decreased by 3.7% to 202,563 units. If the first half of the year is any indication, 2026 isn’t shaping up to be any better. Shipments decreased by 2.9% to 102,847 motorcycles and scooters. That doesn’t take anything away from the impressive milestone reached in Brazil in a relatively short timeframe. Assembling 150,000 motorcycles in just 10 years is no easy feat. It wouldn’t have happened if BMW hadn’t continued to pour money into the plant. This decade, the facility has not only been growing but has also been retooled with the latest equipment to ensure it delivers German-like quality.

15Days Payment Value Rises 50% GS Retail (007070) said on the 4th that both customer payment value and the number of event participants increased following joint marketing between its home shopping unit GS Shop and its supermarket chain GS The Fresh. title: GS Caltex cuts greenhouse gas emissions by 100,000 tons in a year; Heo Se-hong vows push toward centennial status - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Caltex announced Tuesday that its 2025 sustainability report shows total greenhouse gas emissions fell by more than 100,000 tons last year compared with the previous year. The company pursued carbon emission reduction and low-carbon projects under its vision of becoming a "Lower Carbon Refining & Chemical Complex." Through energy efficiency improvements and facility upgrades to strengthen the carbon competitiveness of existing operations, GS Caltex achieved a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. In the low-carbon business segment, the company recorded notable achievements: it became the first in Asia to obtain RecyClass certification covering the entire value chain for end-of-life vehicle (ELV) plastic recycling, and it ranked first for the second consecutive year in the new energy category of the "Most Admired Companies" survey organized by Korea Management Association Consulting (KMAC). In its 21st sustainability report, published this year, GS Caltex highlighted performance not only in the environmental category but also in social and governance areas. On the social front, the company restructured its safety and health framework to reflect key elements of domestic sustainability disclosure standards, reorganizing it around four pillars: governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and performance. GS Caltex also worked to build an advanced safety culture, including compliance with its Life Saving Golden Rules (LSGR), to prevent serious workplace accidents. In governance, the company strengthened its company-wide ESG framework centered on the ESG Committee. In the digital and AI domain, it reinforced security management strategies for key customer and employee information. At the same time, GS Caltex introduced AiU, an in-house integrated generative AI platform, to improve employee productivity and raise the level of internal data protection. "We will press forward without wavering toward becoming a 100-year company — one that is environmentally responsible, socially trusted, and respected for its transparent governance," said Heo Se-hong, vice chairman and CEO of GS Caltex.

Bengaluru: The Congress on Monday announced four-time Ron MLA G S Patil as its nominee for the post of Assembly Speaker. Patil hails from Lingayat community. title: Keep Your Cemetery Running (and the Zombies Out) in Zombie Graveyard Simulator - news.xbox.com
content: If you’re just starting your journey in Zombie Graveyard Simulator, here’s our first piece of advice: don’t let the peaceful daytime fool you. A well-organized cemetery is your best defense when night falls and trust us, you’ll appreciate every upgrade once the zombies start pouring in. We’re excited that you can jump into Zombie Graveyard Simulator today on Xbox Series X|S, and even more excited that you’re getting much more than the original launch experience. Since the game’s debut on PC, we’ve continued expanding it with major content updates inspired by community feedback, and all of those improvements are included from day one on Xbox. One of my favorite additions is the Stone Quarry & Workshop. Thanks to this update, you can mine different types of stone, craft your own gravestones, and develop an entirely new production chain that makes your cemetery feel even more like a living business. The more self-sufficient your operation becomes, the easier it is to keep growing. The world also became much bigger thanks to Expeditions. Rather than spending every day inside the cemetery gates, you’ll answer distress calls, venture into new locations, complete unique objectives, and return with valuable rewards that help expand your business back home. It completely changes the rhythm of the game and offers a welcome break from your daily routine. We’ve also continued adding systems that make your cemetery feel more alive. The Chapel Expansion introduces new buildings, employees, and activities that improve both efficiency and atmosphere, while dynamic weather effects make every day look a little different. Updates like High Stakes & Hot Ashes introduced new cremation mechanics, custom urns, delivery systems, and additional progression paths, giving you even more ways to grow your cemetery exactly the way you want. If you’re looking for a few beginner tips, we’d recommend focusing on your daytime economy before investing heavily in combat. A profitable cemetery means more money for stronger weapons and better defenses. Don’t overlook upgrades that improve your daily workflow, either – saving just a few minutes every in-game day adds up over time. And when you do head into battle each night, remember that good barricade placement can often be just as valuable as having a bigger gun. Perhaps one of the game’s biggest additions, Expeditions, came directly from players asking to explore beyond the cemetery walls. That conversation with the community has shaped nearly every major update we’ve released, from the Stone Quarry & Workshop to new progression systems and quality-of-life improvements. Whether you’re here for the relaxing management gameplay, the satisfaction of building a thriving cemetery, or the thrill of surviving another night against the undead, there’s never been a better time to jump in. Zombie Graveyard Simulator is available now on Xbox Series X|S, and we can’t wait to see how you build and defend your very own cemetery.

RKLB stock jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday, with shares also up nearly 2% overnight. In a recent BBC interview, Beck said commercial launch remains exceptionally difficult despite billions of dollars in investment. “Despite billions of dollars and over 100 companies trying, there has actually only been two companies to pop out the other end,” with a regular and reliable launch service, he said, in a discussion that also touched on Rocket Lab’s rivalry with SpaceX. “Launch and a commercial company doing launch still remains extremely rare,” Beck added. Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Pointing to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 and Starlink model, Beck added: “They’re able to do all those things. And we’re able to do those too.” William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently named Rocket Lab and Blue Origin among the strongest challengers to SpaceX, though he said SpaceX still holds more than 90% of the launch market. Rocket Lab is advancing its competitive vertical integration strategy through its $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications, which would add a global network, spectrum, and recurring satellite service revenue. The company recently completed a full-duration burn of its Archimedes Vacuum engine, an important step toward the first flight of its reusable Neutron rocket. Rocket Lab said it was “critical preparation for Neutron’s first flight.” Beck has told Stocktwits earlier that Rocket Lab is “pushing very hard” to launch Neutron by the fourth quarter of 2026, while cautioning that the challenge is not merely reaching orbit but proving the rocket can return and be reused. “If we just had to go up, it’s super easy, we’d be in orbit by now,” he previously said. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes. title: Is BMW Working on an M 1300 GS? All Signs Point to Yes - inkl
content:
BMW's R 1300 GS is the brand's best-selling motorcycle, and for good reason; it's bloody amazing. It has been the most popular BMW for years, so how could the Bavarian brand further expand its dominance? Well, it could make an M version. As reported by SpeedWeek, it looks like BMW is making an M 1300 GS, which would become the brand's flagship off-road motorcycle. If this comes as a surprise to you, you're not alone. Historically, the 'M' badge has been reserved for BMW's sportiest road-focused vehicles, with 'M' referring to motorsport. The exact shape an M 1300 GS would take is still unknown, but thanks to some spy shots, we have a few clues. In the spy shots, the bikes are under tarpaulins while being transported, but it looks like they're in the later stages of development. What's clear from the photos is that the M badge and features that come with it don't intend to turn the 1300 GS into a road-going phenom, but rather expand on its already impressive off-road capabilities. The bikes have 21-inch front wheels and 18-inch rear wheels, which are fitted with Metzeler Karoo tires, which tell you all you need to know about the terrain this model is intended to perform on. It also looks like there's longer suspension and a redesigned support for the swingarm. The dead giveaway for this bike is the blue 'M' calipers, which should bring more stopping power than the bike's standard BMW-branded, although Brembo-manufactured, calipers. As for the powerplant, it appears as though the 1,300 cc water-cooled boxer remains unchanged, barring an 'M' insignia on the cylinder head covers. That said, with 145 hp and a bonkers 110 lb-ft of torque on tap, I don't think anyone will lose sleep over power gains for off-road use. Cosmetically, it's unclear from the pictures how far BMW will go in terms of an M makeover. Price too remains a mystery, but a BMW M 1000 RR is around $15,000 more than the standard model, whereas an M 1000 R is around $5,500 more, so I'd say it wouldn't be unreasonable to think an M 1300 GS could be $10,000 to 15,000 more than a standard R 1300 GS. title: At $11,799, Could This 1978 Mazda RX-7 GS Make You Go Hmmm? - Jalopnik
content: With no new rotary-powered cars currently on offer, people wanting to get in on the Dorito-shaped piston scene need to look to used cars like today's Nice Price or No Dice RX-7. Considering it's now a classic, let's decide if this Wankel is worth our time. In America, bigger is almost always better. We have bigger dinner plates than do most of the rest of the world. We also have bigger refrigerators to hold all that food needed to fill those bigger plates. That necessitates a larger kitchen to house the big fridge, demanding a bigger house around that, and likely a comparatively large driveway leading to that big-ass house. That super-sizing could make any normal-sized car or truck parked on the property seem dinky by comparison. In such a case, the mega-big six-door, lifted, and wide-tired 2006 Ford F350 we looked at last Friday would be the perfect accompaniment to any such oversized McMansion. Unfortunately for its builder/seller, a $55,000 asking price proved too large for most of our tastes. That was obvious in the comments and the extremely overwhelming 90% 'No Dice' loss the fancy Ford suffered in the vote. For the longest time, the Ford Motor Company maintained a relationship with Japan's Mazda Motors. Ford sold some massaged Mazdas as Mercury models, and shared its popular Explorer—albeit only in two-door form—with their Asian partners. At no time, however, did Ford ever sell any of Mazda's Wankel-engined products as its own. In fact, aside from NSU and a dalliance by Citroën that actually drove the company to bankruptcy, Mazda has pretty much gone it alone in cheerleading the rotary engine. Perhaps the most famous and beloved model to carry the triangle piston torch is the RX-7, and today we're looking at a fairly unmolested 120,000-mile 1978 GS edition to see what all the fuss is about. This Spark Yellow over beige vinyl RX-7 hails from the model's first year on the market. It entered the U.S. market replacing the Cosmo, becoming Mazda's sole rotary offering in North America over three ensuing models and its RX-8 replacement. According to the seller, they have owned the car for 13 years, and it came with a fresh build of its 12A two-rotor motor at that time. That 1146cc Wankel put out a laudable 100 horsepower when new. Per the ad, this one has a Racing Beat header and exhaust, so perhaps it makes a couple more ponies. Everything looks stock under the sloping hood, although a missing belt on what looks to be an air-injection pump does raise questions. Backing the engine up is a five-speed manual transmission driving the solid rear axle. Braking is by discs in the front and drums in the rear, masked by handsome factory four-spoke alloy wheels. Those wheels look to be in great condition, as does the bodywork atop them. Age has taken its toll on the matte black paint on the windscreen pillars and license plate lamp housings, but aside from those minor issues, it's difficult to tell the car from new. Unfortunately, the ad doesn't say whether it drives as well as it looks. One thing that can be gleaned from the pictures in the ad is that the car's interior has not staved off Father Time as well as the exterior has. 1970s plastics don't have the same mojo as modern ones do, a fact made obvious by the cracked dashboard, broken door lever surrounds, and split seam in the driver's seat. Additionally, there are faded window cranks, worn silver paint on the dash separator, and a tear in the passenger-side door cover. Do any of those issues kill this Mazda's appeal? Probably not. Taken as a whole, though, the interior's flaws should offer some wiggle room in negotiating a deal on the car. Replacement parts for these cars are going to be next to impossible to obtain, after all, so its current condition is likely going to have to be lived with by its next owner. One final note about the interior is the stereo, as it's in stereo, with a more modern unit having been placed in the dash under the factory-installed one. That's kind of weird. In the plus column, this is a GS model and so comes with a sunroof. That's a glass panel, which the seller claims is a fairly rare inclusion. Aside from the stereo and the exhaust, this SA RX-7 appears to be completely stock and in very decent condition. It also carries a clean title and will come with some original literature and a few maintenance receipts. That's everything you might expect from a well-cared-for car. To take possession of this RX-7, there is the small matter of the $11,799 the seller is asking for it. That, they warn, is the only deal they are willing to entertain, as trades are off the table. Additionally, they only want to deal with serious inquiries, so low-ballers and shenanigan-eers need not apply. What do you think about this tidy if flawed RX-7 when its $11,799 asking price is taken into account? Does that seem fair for the car as it's presented in its ad? title: Banned Chhatra League ex-GS Ajoy Kar shown arrested in July Uprising murder case - The Business Standard
content: A Dhaka court today (3 August) ordered that former general secretary of the now-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League, Ajoy Kar Khokon, be shown arrested in a murder case over the killing of Md Nazmul Mia during the July Uprising. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jamshed Alam passed the order after hearing a petition filed by the investigation officer of the case. Md Mizanur Rahman, sub-inspector of the prosecution division, confirmed the matter. Police had filed the application on 30 July, with the hearing held today in Ajoy Kar's presence. According to the petition, investigators found evidence of Ajoy Kar's involvement through witness statements and other findings during the investigation. Police argued that he should remain in custody to prevent any threat to public safety. Lawyers for the accused, including Obaidul Islam, Shamim Al Sohag Saiful and Zakir Hossain, opposed the petition, while the prosecution supported it. After hearing both sides, the court granted the application. Following the order, defence lawyer Obaidul Islam said Ajoy Kar has now been shown arrested in three separate cases. He alleged that the latest order was contrary to a High Court directive barring authorities from showing his client arrested in new cases. According to the case statement, Awami League leaders and activists launched armed attacks in Dhanmondi, Mohammadpur and Lalmatia on 4 August 2024 in an attempt to suppress the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement. The case alleges that attackers hurled crude bombs and opened fire near Dhanmondi Hawkers Market at around noon, fatally shooting Md Nazmul Mia. He was declared dead after being taken to a nearby hospital. A colleague of the victim later filed the murder case with Mohammadpur Police Station, naming several accused along with 400 to 500 unidentified individuals. Ajoy Kar was arrested in Dhaka's Gulshan on 23 September 2025 in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act and has remained in jail since. title: 20 MLAs inducted into Karnataka cabinet; GS Patil to be Speaker - The Tribune
content: In a deft move, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday inducted 20 ministers in the first expansion of his cabinet since taking charge of the top post. Many of the faces are new with a mix of caste and regional arithmetics essential to the southern state. SouthAsians & Diaspora The expansion strengthens the Shivakumar cabinet that took charge of the state back in June. The influential Vokkaliga leader had replaced Siddaramaiah in a leadership change that had long been the subject of a power tussle in Karnataka. Maps With the latest round of expansion, the cabinet strength rises from 14 to 34. The new leaders include P M Narendraswamy (Malavalli), Shivaraj Tangadagi (Kanakagiri), Rudrappa Lamani (Haveri), K S Basavanthappa (Mayakonda), B Nagendra (Ballari rural), T Raghumoourthy (Challakere), B Z Zameer Ahmed Khan (Chamarajpet), Rizwan Arshad (Shivajinagar), Santosh Lad (Kalaghatagi), Madhu Bangarappa (Soraba), among others. G S Patil has been chosen as the new speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, while A S Ponnanna will serve as the deputy speaker. The expansion marks the comeback of former Scheduled Tribes welfare minister B Nagendra. A former BJP leader, who had moved to the Congress in 2018, Nagendra had resigned from the cabinet in 2024 over charges linked to the Valmiki Development Corporation scam. Besides, two minority faces are also part of the expansion—B Z Zameer Ahmed Khan and Rizwan Arshad. Children of three former chief ministers are now part of Shivakumar’s Cabinet. They are Yathindra Siddaramaiah (already a minister), Kumar Bangarappa (son of S Bangarappa) and Ajay Singh (son of N Dharam Singh). Incidentally, six of these 20 new ministers were part of the previous government led by Siddaramaiah. Gayathri Shanthegowda, whom the Supreme Court’s recent verdict declared elected from the Chikkamagaluru Local Authorities’ Constituency, will be the lone woman member in the Cabinet. Her election followed the court setting aside BJP’s M K Pranesh’s election to the legislative council in December 2021. Former deputy chief minister Laxman Savadi and Shivalinge Gowda, who joined the Congress from the BJP and JD(S), respectively, ahead of the 2023 assembly polls, are also becoming ministers this time. This much-awaited cabinet expansion aims to maintain social and regional representation, including adequate representation for AHINDA communities, women and younger legislators. The leadership is also seeking to strike a balance between legislators considered close to Shivakumar and those aligned with Siddaramaiah. AHINDA  politics refers to a powerful social and electoral coalition in Karnataka representing ‘Alpasankhyataru’ (minorities), ‘Hindulidavaru’ (backward classes), and ‘Dalitaru’ (dalits). The expansion was expected to take place earlier but was delayed as the Congress leadership worked to strike a balance between experienced leaders and first-time ministers while ensuring equitable representation across Karnataka’s regions and communities. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Shivakumar urged disappointed legislators to remain patient, saying it was “not possible to accommodate everyone” in the ministry. Recalling his own  political journey, he said he too had once missed out on a cabinet berth before eventually becoming a minister. “Similarly, we will ensure that everyone gets an opportunity in the future,” he said. His remarks came after Congress MLA Yashwantrayagouda V Patil resigned after missing out on a cabinet berth, while Belur MLA Gopalakrishna is expected to follow suit, according to sources. More than 15 disgruntled legislators also held a closed-door meeting at senior leader P V Jayachandra’s residence in Bengaluru to discuss their next course of action. Sources said senior leaders, including H K Patil and Dinesh Gundu Rao, attended the meeting. title: GS Caltex gives employees’ families inside look at energy business - The Korea Herald
content:
Business GS Caltex gives employees’ families inside look at energy business GS Caltex said Monday it invited employees’ families to its Seoul headquarters for its annual Family Day on Friday, offering a hands-on look at the company’s workplace and energy business. Held at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu under the theme “Energy to the Future,” the event aimed to help families better understand employees’ work and build a stronger connection with the company. Participants explored interactive exhibits on GS Caltex’s energy operations and digital technologies. At the “Energy Value Chain Adventure” booth, they played a game developed by the company’s Digital & AI Transformation Center to show how crude oil is procured, refined and delivered to customers. Visitors also experienced mixed-reality and virtual-reality content featuring the company’s Yeosu refinery, including safety training programs used by employees at the site. Other activities included AI-powered board games, robot soccer, motion-sensing sports, eco-bag and key ring making, and family photo sessions. GS Caltex Vice Chair Hur Sae-hong greeted employees’ families and thanked them for their support. “I hope Family Day helped our employees’ families better understand GS Caltex and their parents’ workplace, while taking pride in what they do,” Hur said. “I also hope the experience becomes a cherished memory and inspires the children to pursue their dreams and become the energy our future society needs.” Lee orders ‘swift, decisive’ merger of military academies to prevent another coup President asks Unification Ministry to weigh whether to call N. title: GS Caltex Holds 'Family Day' with Vice Chairman Huh Sae-hong - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Held on July 31 at GS Tower
GS Caltex Honorary Employees for a Day GS Caltex said on the 3rd that Vice Chairman Huh Sae-hong attended an event inviting the families of executives and employees and expressed his gratitude. The "Family Day," held on the 31st of last month at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, under the theme "Energy to the Future," was arranged so that the spouses and children of executives and employees could tour the workplace in person and experience GS Caltex's energy business. Employee families selected through advance application took part in an office tour to look around the actual work spaces and working environment. After receiving GS Caltex honorary employee ID cards, they moved to the Family Day venue to experience the main programs. First, at the "Great Energy Value Chain Expedition" booth, participants took time to understand the value chain of the energy business, from crude oil purchasing to product production and sales, through game content developed directly by the GS Caltex DAX (Digital & AI Transformation) Center. They also viewed a panoramic view of the GS Caltex Yeosu plant using mixed reality (MR) and virtual reality (VR), and experienced MR- and VR-based safety training content currently in use at actual sites. Participants also enjoyed a variety of programs, including experience programs using digital technology such as artificial intelligence (AI) baduk and omok, mini robot soccer, and motion-recognition sports, as well as eco-bag and keyring making and family photo shoots. Vice Chairman Huh, who attended the event, offered encouragement, saying, "I hope today's experience will remain a pleasant memory and lead to a good opportunity to nurture dreams going forward," and "I cheer you on to grow into the energy that future society truly needs." Meanwhile, GS Caltex operates various family-friendly programs to support the work-life balance of its executives and employees. title: GS Caltex Hosts Family Day for Employees - GS칼텍스 미디어허브
content:
GS칼텍스

                                    2026.08.03 GS Caltex (Board Chair & CEO, GS Caltex / Vice Chairman, GS Group, Saehong Hur) announced that it hosted Family Day for employees and their families on July 31 at GS Tower in Gangnam, Seoul. Family Day, held under the theme “Energy to the Future,” gave employees’ families an opportunity to visit the workplace and experience GS Caltex’s energy business firsthand. More than a company tour, the event helped families become more familiar with the company while fostering pride and a sense of belonging. Selected through a pre-registration process, participants got a look at where their family members work before receiving honorary employee ID cards and taking part in the day’s programs. At the main event venue, a variety of interactive booths gave participants a clear, engaging introduction to GS Caltex’s energy business and digital technologies. At the “Energy Value Chain Adventure” booth, they learned how the company’s value chain works—from crude oil procurement to product manufacturing and sales—through game-based content developed by GS Caltex’s DAX (Digital & AI Transformation) Center. Participants also explored GS Caltex’s Yeosu Complex via MR (Mixed Reality) and VR (Virtual Reality) and experienced the same safety training content used on site to see how digital technologies support workplace safety. The event also featured a variety of activities based on digital technology, including AI Baduk & Omok, mini robot soccer, and motion-recognition sports, as well as activities for the whole family, such as eco-bag and keyring making and photo sessions. During the event, CEO Saehong Hur welcomed everyone and thanked them for their support. He said, “I hope this Family Day has helped our employees’ families better understand what their parents do at GS Caltex and take pride in their work,” adding, “Today’s experience will, I hope, remain a fond memory and inspire them to dream big as they grow.” GS Caltex also offers a range of family-friendly programs to support employees’ work-life balance. In recognition of these efforts, the company received the Korean government’s Family-Friendly Certification in 2023. GS Caltex (Board Chair & CEO, GS Caltex / Vice Chairman, GS Group, Saehong Hur) announced on July 16 that it has successfully completed its 2026 first-half turnaround (TA) at the Yeosu Complex. A turnaround is a large-scale scheduled maintenance project during which refinery and petrochemical operations are temporarily suspended to allow for intensive inspection of major production facilities. The work includes servicing production facilities and replacing aging parts and consumables to help ensure safe and efficient operations. GS Caltex (Board Chair & CEO, GS Caltex / Vice Chairman, GS Group, Saehong Hur) announced that it had signed a comprehensive memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Veolia, a global environmental solutions company, on April 3 to innovate utility operations and strengthen sustainability at its Yeosu Complex.
